Biome CLI v2.6.3

2.6.3

Patch Changes

  • #12275 807e616 Thanks @​dyc3! - Added the new nursery rule noArraySortForMinMax, which reports sorting an array only to read its smallest or largest value. Use Math.min() or Math.max() instead.

    const minimum = array.toSorted((a, b) => a - b)[0];

  • #12432 cf61682 Thanks @​dyc3! - Added the nursery rule noBooleanSortComparator, which reports sort comparators that return a boolean instead of a number. For example, array.sort((a, b) => a > b) never puts the first item before the second, so the array isn't sorted correctly.

  • #12304 b4654c5 Thanks @​dyc3! - Added the new nursery rule noEagerArrayMethodsInLoops, which reports .map() and .filter() calls in the header of for...of loops. These calls build a new array that is only used by the loop.

    for (const name of users.map((user) => user.name)) {
  console.log(name);
}

  • #12121 66c3791 Thanks @​dyc3! - Added the nursery rule noNewRequire, which disallows calling require with new, such as new require("app-header").

  • #12316 34b520d Thanks @​dyc3! - Added the new nursery rule noObsoleteAttributes, which disallows obsolete attributes on HTML elements and suggests what to use instead.

    <table bgcolor="#ffffff" cellpadding="5"></table>

  • #12258 cce2385 Thanks @​dyc3! - Added the nursery rule noPathConcat, which disallows building file paths and URLs by joining strings to __dirname, __filename, import.meta.dirname, import.meta.filename, or import.meta.url.

    const fullPath = __dirname + "/foo.js"; // reported

  • #12287 e12ad78 Thanks @​dyc3! - Added the new nursery rule noPlaywrightNthMethods, which disallows selecting Playwright elements by position with first(), last(), and nth(). A test that relies on the position of an element can act on a different element when the page changes.

    await page.locator("button").first().click();

  • #12343 62ad123 Thanks @​vibbix! - Added the nursery rule noSelfNestedLayer, which disallows nesting a cascade layer inside a layer with the same name. Layer names inside an @layer block are relative to it, so the inner layer below creates the sublayer components.components instead of adding to components.

Updates `fallow` from 3.34.1 to 3.37.0
Release notes

Sourced from fallow's releases.

v3.37.0: resumable mutation runs, CSS classes from template files, and signed Windows binaries

Features

  • fallow health --css reads server-side template files as class references. Fallow now reads .liquid, .njk, .hbs, .handlebars, .twig and .blade.php files, and each class-like word in them counts as used. A class that only a Shopify Liquid section applies is no longer an unreferenced-css-class. A class prefix before a {{ echo, as in grid--{{ columns }}, also counts. The {{ rule also applies to .vue, .html, .md and .astro sources with dynamic class syntax, so these sources can report fewer classes. Use the new top-level markupExtensions key to add other template extensions, for example ["tpl", "erb"]. These files do not join source discovery, so they never become unused files. Thanks @​james2doyle for the report. (#3917)

  • The npm package now ships rule-pack-schema.json. Point the $schema of a rule pack at ./node_modules/fallow/rule-pack-schema.json to get a schema that matches the installed version. The package also exports the file as fallow/rule-pack-schema.json. Thanks @​hckhanh for the report and @​tahodev for the change. (#3851)

  • An interrupted fallow mutation run keeps its finished results, and --resume continues it. Each run writes each killed and retry-confirmed survived mutant to .fallow/mutation/journal.jsonl when its result is final, also with --no-cache. fallow mutation --resume reuses these results and runs only the other mutants. When the journal comes from other inputs, the run exits 2 with FALLOW_MUTATION_RESUME_MISMATCH and names each input that differs. A resumed mutant has resumed: true, and the report has a resume object. A complete run removes the journal, and a partial run keeps it. (#3783)

Changed

  • A bare machine run that exits 0 on a failing gate now says so on stderr. Bare fallow in a machine format exits 0 on findings, but fallow dead-code --format json exits 1 on the same findings. Before, nothing showed why. Now the run prints one stderr line, also under --quiet, that names each failing findings gate and the flag that enforces it. The exit code and stdout do not change. Thanks @​Smrtnyk for the report. (#3826)

  • The exit-code contract no longer says that exit 0 means a clean run. fallow schema (exit_codes), the fallow skill and the npm README now say that 0 means no enforced gate failed. Exit 1 means findings, not a tool failure. A bare machine run gates on findings only with --fail-on-issues. To see a failing gate that did not set the exit code, read gate_outcomes.

  • fallow mutation gives no mutant for a pure condition whose only effect is a logging call. An if statement such as if (count > 0) { console.info("Items", count); } no longer gives mutants. The condition must be pure, and each branch must hold only console.* or debug(...) calls with pure arguments. In a file that declares or imports console or debug, the conditions that call that name keep their mutants. (#3719)

Bug fixes

  • thin-wrapper and duplicate-prop-shape set to error now fail the gates. At error, these rules count in issue totals, the dead-code and audit gates, and CI reports. A rule at warn does not fail a gate, also with --fail-on-issues. Thanks @​luciocabrera for the report. (#3867)

  • A CommonJS postcss.config.cjs no longer reports its module.exports keys as unused exports. When a plugin credits only default for a CommonJS module, Fallow now credits every key of module.exports. The fix applies to the CommonJS config files of all plugins that read the default export. Thanks @​waldoluisribeiro for the report. (#3876)

  • fallow security resolves a string enum member in the same module. Fallow no longer reports a template literal such as `<meta name="${MetaName.BUILD_NUMBER}">` that goes to an HTML sink as non-literal HTML. Enums and constants that you import from another module stay unresolved. The first run after the update parses all files again. Thanks @​Smrtnyk for the report. (#3854)

  • Component export queries no longer stop type-aware refinement for the whole run. Fallow now gives Vue, Astro, Svelte and MDX query files an unsupported-syntax abstention. Supported TypeScript and JavaScript queries in the same batch continue to resolve. (#3763)

  • fallow dead-code follows child_process.fork targets built from the module directory. A file that fork(path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "child.ts")) starts is no longer an unused file. path.resolve, __dirname, import.meta.dirname and a constant that holds the module directory also work. Thanks @​VariableVince for the report. (#3919)

  • Fallow now reads config values from a same-file constant. A config can keep part of its value in a top-level constant, for example projects: [UNIT]. Fallow now uses the value of the constant, so the setup files of such a Vitest project are no longer unused files. The fix applies to all plugins that read config files. Thanks @​Smrtnyk for the report. (#3852)

  • fallow dead-code no longer reports a class member as unused when an array pattern or a getter on a held object is its only read. An array pattern around an object pattern, such as const [{ m }] = [service], now credits the member. Fallow also credits the member for a src.k.m read through a getter on an object literal that a variable holds. Both forms now credit the member without --type-aware. (#3799)

  • Package scripts and CI steps that run a local shell helper now credit the commands of that helper. For bash scripts/build.sh or ./scripts/release.sh, Fallow reads the helper without running it. A binary that the helper runs makes its package used, and a file that the helper runs with tsx or node becomes an entry. Fallow follows nested helpers and literal cd steps. Thanks @​VariableVince for the report in #3918. (#3886)

  • fallow dead-code now credits a store member that a helper reads through a store alias declared in a function body. An alias such as type X = ReturnType<typeof useXStore> in a function body or block now credits the store member. An inner type of the same name still shadows the alias. (#3550)

  • Deeply nested defaults in an object pattern no longer make extraction hang. In a declaration such as const { k: { k: { m } = s } = s } = s, the work doubled at each level of nesting. A step budget now bounds the walk of one declaration.

  • fallow dead-code now credits Expo config plugins that come from a local array binding. An app config can hold its plugins list in a top-level const or let. Fallow now reads that list, its spreads, and push, unshift or splice calls on it. An expo object with a type assertion, such as satisfies ExpoConfig, now also counts. (#3883)

  • --production --type-aware no longer credits an export that only a test file uses. A type-aware reference from a file outside the analysis scope no longer removes a dead-code finding. Thanks @​Smrtnyk for the report. (#3869)

  • Audit cleanup preserves unrelated Git worktree registrations. When Fallow removes old snapshots, it keeps each user worktree registered while its directory is temporarily unavailable. (#3884)

  • Extraction is no longer slow on malformed input. Incomplete script and style tags in Astro and incomplete template tags in Vue and Angular no longer cause repeated scans. An unfinished multiline import or export in MDX no longer makes the parser run again for each line. CODEOWNERS lookups with long patterns no longer use too much memory or time. Results and source offsets do not change.

  • Type-aware refinement on the tsrs backend no longer fails on public APIs with many non-generic interfaces. The semantic sidecar now asks for type arguments only on type references. tsrs now gives the same result as typescript-go. Thanks @​Smrtnyk for the report and the reproduction. (#3872)

  • Programmatic and MCP audits no longer show their base snapshot in git worktree list. The API, the MCP audit tool and the pull-request decision output now remove the Git registration of the base snapshot, as fallow audit does. They also remove snapshots that a stopped process left behind. (#3885)

Release notes

v13.6.0

13.6.0 (2026-10-27)

Full Changelog

We expect this release to ship in the DevTools of Chrome 159, and to PageSpeed Insights within a week.

New contributors

Thanks to our new contributors 👽🐷🐰🐯🐻!

  • Nikolay Vitkov @​Lightning00Blade
  • MohammadHossein Jahanbakhsh @​MHJahanbakhsh
  • Rafe Blandford @​rafeblandford
  • Roman @​gameroman
  • Ivan Akulov @​iamakulov
  • Francesco Marinoni Moretto @​frmoretto

Notable Changes

  • CLI bulk URL auditing: The CLI now supports auditing multiple URLs sequentially in a single command—either by passing multiple URL arguments or via --url-file (with --fail-fast to abort on the first failure) (#17404). Default report filenames now include the URL pathname (<hostname>-<pathname>_<date>) to avoid collisions across pages on the same host (#17405, #17423).
  • Lantern simulation improvements: Upgraded trace_engine (0.0.66 and 0.0.67) and updated request/graph modeling to improve simulation accuracy (#17307, #17379):
    • Network & protocol modeling: Treated HTTP/3 connections as multiplexed, credited consumed H2 overflow bytes across simulation steps, excluded connectionless requests from active connection counts, and improved origin RTT/throughput estimation and redirect handling (#17415).
    • Dependency graph & metrics: Added v8.compileModule and v8.evaluateModule trace event attribution, used protocol renderBlocking status for render-blocking priority (#16869), used FCP graphs when text LCP occurs in the same frame as FCP, and fixed simulated LCP breakdown calculations (#17269) and trace-mode navigation/URL handling (#17431, #17433).
  • Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) v0.91: Updated the ard-schema audit and gatherer to the ARD v0.91 specification (ard.json replacing ai-catalog.json), supporting discovery via Link HTTP headers, <link rel="ard">, and /.well-known/ard.json, warning on legacy ai-catalog locations, and displaying the ARD spec version in the report footer (#17258, #17259, #17260, #17448, #17452).
  • Performance insight numericValue: Performance insight audits now populate numericValue and numericUnit from estimated time or byte savings (#17346), and select the correct navigation when traces contain multiple navigations (#17174).
  • Memory and gathering optimizations: Reduced peak memory usage during runs by streaming traces (ReturnAsStream), reusing script sources from trace events, evicting decoded frame buffers in speedline, and releasing intermediate gatherer and trace engine state (#17286, #17289, #17290, #17407).

  • release retained gatherer and trace engine intermediate state (#17290)
  • populate numericValue on performance insight audits (#17346)

  • baseline: fix getLowDate for high features, move web-features to devDeps (#17283)

Thanks to our new contributors 👽🐷🐰🐯🐻!

  • Nikolay Vitkov @​Lightning00Blade
  • MohammadHossein Jahanbakhsh @​MHJahanbakhsh
  • Rafe Blandford @​rafeblandford
  • Roman @​gameroman

  • Francesco Marinoni Moretto @​frmoretto

Notable Changes

  • CLI bulk URL auditing: The CLI now supports auditing multiple URLs sequentially in a single command—either by passing multiple URL arguments or via --url-file (with --fail-fast to abort on the first failure) (#17404). Default report filenames now include the URL pathname (<hostname>-<pathname>_<date>) to avoid collisions across pages on the same host (#17405, #17423).
  • Lantern simulation improvements: Upgraded trace_engine (0.0.66 and 0.0.67) and updated request/graph modeling to improve simulation accuracy (#17307, #17379):
    • Network & protocol modeling: Treated HTTP/3 connections as multiplexed, credited consumed H2 overflow bytes across simulation steps, excluded connectionless requests from active connection counts, and improved origin RTT/throughput estimation and redirect handling (#17415).
    • Dependency graph & metrics: Added v8.compileModule and v8.evaluateModule trace event attribution, used protocol renderBlocking status for render-blocking priority (#16869), used FCP graphs when text LCP occurs in the same frame as FCP, and fixed simulated LCP breakdown calculations (#17269) and trace-mode navigation/URL handling (#17431, #17433).
  • Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) v0.91: Updated the ard-schema audit and gatherer to the ARD v0.91 specification (ard.json replacing ai-catalog.json), supporting discovery via Link HTTP headers, <link rel="ard">, and /.well-known/ard.json, warning on legacy ai-catalog locations, and displaying the ARD spec version in the report footer (#17258, #17259, #17260, #17448, #17452).
  • Performance insight numericValue: Performance insight audits now populate numericValue and numericUnit from estimated time or byte savings (#17346), and select the correct navigation when traces contain multiple navigations (#17174).
  • Memory and gathering optimizations: Reduced peak memory usage during runs by streaming traces (ReturnAsStream), reusing script sources from trace events, evicting decoded frame buffers in speedline, and releasing intermediate gatherer and trace engine state (#17286, #17289, #17290, #17407).
